question: How many of the main fixed instruments can be found in the Jantar Mantar, Jaipur ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**20**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is an astronomical observatory built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1734.
 
• It contains **20 main fixed instruments** designed for measuring time, tracking celestial bodies, and predicting eclipses.
 
• The instruments include iconic structures such as the **Samrat Yantra (giant sundial)**, Jai Prakash Yantra, and Ram Yantra.
 
• The observatory is recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** for its cultural and scientific significance.
 
• Jantar Mantar showcases the advanced understanding of astronomy and engineering in 18th-century India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samrat Yantra:** It is the largest sundial in the world, with a height of 27 meters, used to measure time with an accuracy of about 2 seconds.
 
• **Jai Prakash Yantra:** A hemispherical instrument used for determining the positions of celestial objects.
 
• **Ram Yantra:** Two cylindrical structures used to measure the altitude and azimuth of celestial bodies.
 
• The Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is one of the five observatories built by Sawai Jai Singh II, the others being in Delhi, Ujjain, Varanasi, and Mathura.
 
• The observatory is an example of the blend of **scientific innovation and architectural brilliance** of its time.
